title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-p19p: TH_2 CBOR bstr wrapping breaks RFC 9528 compliance
description:
## Severity: P0 (breaks protocol interop with all RFC 9528 implementations)

### Summary
Commit 44d394c ("project-LICHEN-worker6-p19p: fix") wraps TH_2 transcript hash inputs in CBOR bstr encoding, but RFC 9528 Appendix C.1.1 test vectors require raw byte concatenation.

### Evidence
- OLD TH_2 (raw concat): `c1d8c6ee4eeb1672d7fcbb44f8d811419739b79b852fce03f527eacdaf6633c4` — **matches RFC 9528 C.1.1**
- NEW TH_2 (CBOR-wrapped): `c6405c154c567466ab1df20369500e540e9f14bd3a796a0652cae66c9061688d` — **diverges**

Verification:
```
g_y = dc88d2d5...b9b29d1c (RFC C.1.1 G_Y)
message_1 = 00005820...237f042d (RFC C.1.1 message_1)

Raw:   SHA-256(g_y || H(message_1))          = c1d8c6ee...  ✓ matches RFC
CBOR:  SHA-256(CBOR(g_y) || CBOR(H(msg1)))   = c6405c15...  ✗ diverges
```

The raw input is 64 bytes (32+32). The CBOR input is 68 bytes (34+34, with 0x58 0x20 bstr headers). Both Python and Rust implementations were changed identically and both are now non-compliant.

### Affected files
- `python/src/lichen/crypto/edhoc.py`: lines 389, 598 — `cbor2.dumps(g_y)` and `cbor2.dumps(self._eph_pk)` + `cbor2.dumps(h_msg1)` should be raw concatenation
- `rust/lichen-oscore/src/edhoc.rs`: lines 415-421 — `encode_bstr` calls in `transcript_2` should be `extend_err`/raw concatenation
- All downstream test vectors (PRK_2e, keystream_2, TH_3, TH_4, PRK_out, PRK_exporter, exporter outputs) are cascade-broken

### Fix
Revert TH_2 input encoding to raw byte concatenation (matching RFC 9528 test vectors). The RFC Section 3.5 text describing CBOR bstr wrapping is ambiguous and contradicted by the normative test vectors in Appendix C.1.1.

### Note
This does NOT mean all transcript hash inputs use raw concatenation — TH_3 and TH_4 already used `encode_bstr` before this commit and may have a different encoding convention. Verify TH_3/TH_4 against RFC test vectors separately.
